title: Project Risk Band Definitions
content:
The AI Financial Underwriting Copilot uses four project-defined
Probability of Default risk bands:

Low Risk:
PD < 5%

Medium Risk:
5% <= PD < 10%

High Risk:
10% <= PD < 20%

Very High Risk:
PD >= 20%

These thresholds are project assumptions for demonstration and
decision-support purposes. They are not regulatory credit-risk
standards and should not be interpreted as universal lending
requirements.

title: Underwriting Decision Engine
content:
The decision engine combines the machine-learning Probability of
Default with deterministic policy results.

Project decision rules:

REJECT:
- Any policy rule is CRITICAL, OR
- predicted PD >= 20%

REVIEW:
- No critical rule exists, but at least one policy rule is WARNING, OR
- predicted PD >= 10%

APPROVE:
- No critical rule,
- no warning rule,
- and predicted PD < 10%.

The decision engine is deterministic. The LLM cannot change,
override, or replace the decision produced by this engine.

title: Policy Rule Status Definitions
content:
Policy rules in the project have four possible statuses:

PASSED:
The observed value does not cross the configured warning or
critical threshold.

WARNING:
The observed value crosses the configured warning threshold but
does not cross the critical threshold.

CRITICAL:
The observed value crosses the configured critical threshold.

NOT_EVALUATED:
The required historical information is unavailable. This status
does not represent a policy violation.

title: Bureau Debt to Credit Policy
content:
BUREAU_DEBT_TO_CREDIT is calculated as total historical bureau debt
divided by total historical bureau credit.

The current project policy configuration uses:

WARNING:
BUREAU_DEBT_TO_CREDIT >= 0.75

CRITICAL:
BUREAU_DEBT_TO_CREDIT >= 0.90

These thresholds are project-specific assumptions derived from
exploratory population analysis. They are not regulatory standards.

title: Installment Repayment Policy
content:
INSTALLMENT_LATE_RATE represents the proportion of historical
installment records where payment occurred after the scheduled date.

Current project thresholds:

WARNING:
INSTALLMENT_LATE_RATE >= 0.25

CRITICAL:
INSTALLMENT_LATE_RATE >= 0.50

INSTALLMENT_UNDERPAYMENT_RATE represents the proportion of
historical installment records where the paid amount was below
the scheduled installment amount.

Current project thresholds:

WARNING:
INSTALLMENT_UNDERPAYMENT_RATE >= 0.25

CRITICAL:
INSTALLMENT_UNDERPAYMENT_RATE >= 0.50

title: SHAP Explanation Guidance
content:
SHAP values describe how the trained model attributes a prediction
to individual features relative to the model's baseline output.

A positive SHAP value means that the feature contributed toward a
higher model output for that applicant.

A negative SHAP value means that the feature contributed toward a
lower model output for that applicant.

SHAP values are model attributions, not causal effects.

SHAP values must not be interpreted as percentage-point changes
in Probability of Default.

title: Historical Data Availability
content:
Historical datasets such as credit-card history and bureau-balance
history are not available for every applicant.

When a historical source is unavailable, the system can mark a
policy rule as NOT_EVALUATED.

Unavailable history must not automatically be interpreted as
negative credit behavior or as a policy violation.

Missing historical information and observed adverse behavior are
different concepts.

title: Model Evaluation Metrics
content:
The final historical-feature HistGradientBoosting model is evaluated
using ROC-AUC, PR-AUC and Brier Score.

ROC-AUC measures ranking ability across classification thresholds.

PR-AUC is especially useful in this project because default cases
are a minority of the population.

Brier Score evaluates the quality of predicted probabilities.

The project does not use classification accuracy as the primary
model-selection criterion.

title: LLM Underwriting Guardrails
content:
The LLM is an explanation and question-answering layer.

The LLM must not:

- calculate a new Probability of Default,
- override the deterministic decision,
- change the risk band,
- invent applicant information,
- treat SHAP attribution as causal,
- use unavailable history as evidence of bad behavior.

The source of truth remains the structured ML, SHAP and policy
outputs produced by the underwriting system.

title: System Architecture
content:
The AI Financial Underwriting Copilot consists of:

Applicant Data
-> Data Validation
-> Feature Engineering
-> ML Risk Model
-> Probability of Default
-> Risk Band
-> SHAP Explainability
-> Policy Engine
-> Decision Engine
-> Grounded LLM
-> Underwriting Report / Natural-Language Q&A.

The LLM is downstream of the deterministic underwriting engine.
